verdicts.rewritten_summary: CNC3 (23 Aug 2024): the PNM Constitution Review Committee rejected adding sexual-orientation protections to the national constitution (decision announced at a special convention); CAISO's Dr Angelique Nixon said the community has 'been waiting far too long for equal rights and protection'. Documents LGBTQ-rights exclusion from the 2024 constitutional-review process.

GlobalGayz (Aug 2012): travel/culture profile stating that although homosexuality is illegal 'the laws are mostly ignored' in practice; describes tourist-facing social scene and island context. Usable as a 2012 non-enforcement baseline; predates the 2018 decriminalisation ruling, so dated for current-law purposes.

PinkNews (21 Nov 2017): first-person appeal by activist Jason Jones during his High Court challenge to T&T's same-sex criminalisation — he faces up to 25 years' imprisonment for consensual sex with an adult male partner; article carries the litigation campaign. Marks the constitutional challenge that put the criminal law in play.

Erasing 76 Crimes (23 Jun 2016): PM Keith Rowley told Parliament (17 Jun 2016) the state must protect all citizens 'regardless of whom they sleep with', while refusing to repeal the same-sex criminal laws; cites Newsday. Documents the reform-refusal gap in official rhetoric as of 2016.

Amnesty International (11 Feb 2025): at least 84 people — mainly gay men and trans women — arrested, arbitrarily detained and prosecuted in Tunis, Hammamet, Sousse and El Kef between 26 Sep 2024 and 31 Jan 2025 on 'public indecency'/morality charges; a 31 Oct 2024 mass conviction drew prison terms up to 4.5 years, upheld on appeal 5 Feb 2025 (four released after reduction). Quantified 2024-25 crackdown evidence.

Cairo 52 country page: Penal Code Article 230 criminalises same-sex conduct with up to 3 years' imprisonment; records enforcement (e.g. Oct 2021 arrest of two transgender women under morality/debauchery provisions) and gaps in legal gender recognition. Primary-law summary for visitor risk.

Intersection Association (Nov 2024): transgender women in Tunisian prisons are processed under their former names and birth gender in detention records, arrest processes and court hearings — systemic identity refusal from detention onward, described as continuous suffering and discrimination inside the prison system. Direct trans-specific custodial-risk evidence.

Cairo 52 (30 Jan 2024): reports the Tunis Court of First Instance's Apr 2023 refusal of legal gender recognition to a transgender man; the court weighed contradictory lower-court judgements (incl. case No. 12304/2018) and found no consistent precedent, leaving recognition unsettled below the Court of Cassation. Shows LGR is court-by-court and often denied.

Human Rights Watch (29 Mar 2016): documents at least seven men prosecuted for consensual same-sex conduct in two cases over six months, all convicted under Penal Code art. 230 (up to 3 years); interviewed detainees reported beatings, forced anal examinations and humiliating treatment by police. Core enforcement-abuse evidence.

Erasing 76 Crimes (27 Sep 2017): Tunisia pledged to the UN to stop forced anal testing in homosexuality cases, but kept the anti-gay law itself; Kapitalis warns the pledge does not decriminalise anything. Shows reform-by-commitment without legal change.

url.claim: Human Rights Watch (Oct 2025): 'Türkiye: Draft Law Threatens LGBT People with Prison' — a proposed penal-code package would effectively criminalise LGBT people with long prison terms.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Human Rights Watch (29 Oct 2025): a draft legislative package would effectively criminalise LGBT people under vague claims of protecting 'the family' and 'public morals' — framing the Erdoğan government has repeatedly used to legitimise stigmatisation; sets the reform backdrop as authoritarian drift. Key legislative-risk evidence for 2025-26.

url.claim: Kaos GL (Feb 2026): 'A major siege' against LGBTI+ people in 2025 - hostility turned into state policy; the LGBTI+ Human Rights Report 2025 ('The Year of the Family: A Major Siege Against LGBTI+ People') documents institutionalised anti-LGBTI policies, hate speech from senior officials, and instructions to public institutions under the 'Year of the Family' banner creating a climate encouraging human-rights violations.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Kaos GL (Feb 2026): the LGBTI+ Human Rights Report 2025 records 313 violations in 2025 — about two-and-a-half times 2024 — dominated by detention (299 detention decisions: 256 on record, 43 off the record), plus systematic privacy attacks; frames hostility turned into state policy. Quantified annual evidence.

url.claim: bianet (Aug 2025): Istanbul police detain ~20 trans women for ID checks amid profiling concerns - stopped on the street, while shopping or in cafés in Beyoğlu, held at Taksim Şehit Haşim Usta Police Station and released after 'General Information Gathering' (GBT) background checks; legal experts argue GBT checks violate ECHR Article 5; one detainee: 'They didn't fine us, but they documented us. The new law hasn't even passed yet, but they're already enforcing it on us.'
